summary: The milestone completed 12 experiments in 2 minutes, and 6 were compute-bound. The ARC live-path target-validated mechanic-route causal canary was the longest listed compute-bound task, but the supplied data has no phase breakdown that explains why.
bottlenecks_identified: The disk-mtime reconstruction ranks experiment elapsed times but has no task-phase detail, so it cannot attribute the longest compute-bound duration to setup, model loading, inference, or teardown.
GPU monitoring is not correlated to experiment intervals, so utilization efficiency during compute-bound tasks cannot be graded from the supplied data.
No loaded-model count or runner-selection receipt is available, so the data cannot establish whether any task ran 2 or more models in parallel or missed an eligible DualGPURunner dispatch.
improvements_suggested: Record phase timestamps and task identifiers for every compute-bound experiment.
Attach GPU utilization samples to each compute-bound task from launch through completion.
Record loaded-model count and runner selection, and select DualGPURunner only when 2 or more models are loaded in parallel.
Keep synthesis-only tasks on the non-GPU path and exclude their expected GPU idleness from alerts.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add task-correlated phase and GPU telemetry for compute-bound experiments.
Emit loaded-model-count and runner-selection receipts before compute starts.
Dispatch parallel multi-model workloads across both GPUs with DualGPURunner while retaining one-GPU dispatch for single-model work.
meta_reflection: The reconstructed timing is sufficient to rank the listed work but not to identify causal runtime waste. The next retrospective will be more actionable if task-scoped phase, GPU, model-count, and dispatch evidence is captured during execution.
